title: Grow up, hold the anchor, meet Melchizedek

passage.why: The author pauses to rouse dull hearers (5:11-6:12), steadies them with God's oath (6:13-20), then opens the deep teaching he promised: Jesus a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.

readAloud: Consequently, he is able to save to the uttermost those who draw near to God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them. (Hebrews 7:25)
readAloudNote: ESV, checked this session. A footnote offers 'forever' for 'to the uttermost'.
setting: Melchizedek appears twice in the Old Testament: as king of Salem and priest of God Most High who blessed Abraham and received a tenth (Genesis 14:18-20), and in Psalm 110:4, where the coming king is 'a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek'. Hebrews joins the two.

sections.heading: Milk and solid food
sections.body: 'You have become dull of hearing... You need milk, not solid food' (5:11-12). Maturity is 'for those who have their powers of discernment trained by constant practice to distinguish good from evil' (5:14). Growth comes by practice, not just information.

sections.heading: The hardest warning (6:4-8)
sections.body: 'It is impossible, in the case of those who have once been enlightened... and then have fallen away, to restore them again to repentance' (6:4-6). Read it next to 6:9: 'in your case, beloved, we feel sure of better things.' The three readings from session 1 apply here most of all. Bring this passage to your pastor.

sections.heading: An anchor behind the curtain
sections.body: God swore by himself to Abraham, so that 'by two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge might have strong encouragement to hold fast to the hope set before us. We have this as a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul, a hope that enters into the inner place behind the curtain, where Jesus has gone as a forerunner on our behalf' (6:18-20).

sections.heading: Why Melchizedek matters
sections.body: Abraham gave him a tenth and was blessed by him, so Melchizedek is greater than Levi, who was 'in the loins' of Abraham (7:4-10). Jesus is priest 'not on the basis of a legal requirement concerning bodily descent, but by the power of an indestructible life' (7:16). Levitical priests died and were replaced; 'he holds his priesthood permanently, because he continues forever' (7:24), and 'he always lives to make intercession' (7:25).

sections.heading: Who was Melchizedek?
sections.body: Most read him as a real king-priest in Abraham's day, whose missing genealogy in Genesis makes him a type of Christ (7:3, 'resembling the Son of God'). Some early and modern readers think he was a pre-incarnate appearance of the Son. The text says 'resembling', which favours the first reading.

observe: In 5:11-14, what marks the immature and what marks the mature?
Read 6:4-6 and 6:9-12 together. How does the author speak to the same people in both?
Make two columns from chapter 7: the Levitical priests and Jesus. What is 'better' about him?

words.note: Sluggish or lazy. The same word reappears in 6:12, 'that you may not be sluggish': the problem is a slow heart, not a slow mind.
One who runs ahead to open the way, like a scout or the first boat to reach the harbour (6:20).
Completely and for all time: both senses sit in the phrase (7:25).

crossRefs.note: A priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.
God swears by himself to Abraham.
Christ Jesus who intercedes for us: your reading spine.

reflect: Where am I still on milk, knowing much but practising little?
What storm in my life right now needs the anchor of 6:19?
How does it change today's prayers to know Jesus 'always lives to make intercession' for me?

practice.name: Train by practice
practice.how: Pick one discernment you face this week, at home or at Eden. Before deciding, write the good, the evil and the merely convenient options, and pray 7:25 over it. That is 5:14's 'constant practice' in small form.

pray: Adoration: a priest by the power of an indestructible life. Confession: sluggishness of heart. Thanksgiving: an anchor that holds. Supplication: for maturity, and for the people I lead.
journalPrompts: What did I learn about God this week, from the reading or from life?
Where did I see Jesus as better this week than the thing I was leaning on?
What question did this passage raise that I want to bring to my pastor or Micah?
